# enumeration-drift-fixtures.txt — labelled expected-verdict set for the enumeration-drift check
#
# PROVENANCE. These cases are the labelled fixture set of the enumeration <-> population
# drift check (core/deploy/tools/check-enumeration-drift.py, deploy.sh Check 83), written
# with the check by its introducing release. Case 1 is the seeded mismatch the check must
# flag, and case 2 its near-miss — the same document as a true `subset-of` — which it must
# not flag; together they are the control arm the check's acceptance criteria require.
# Each remaining case pins one rule the tool's module docstring states, so a regression
# names the rule it broke. The list below names the rule each case pins. It is not a sweep
# of the docstring: a rule it does not name is not pinned by this set, and the rules found
# unpinned so far are named at its end.
#
# FORMAT (case-block, because a marked enumeration is irreducibly multi-line):
#   --- <EXPECT> <RELATION> <label>
#   POPULATION: <repo-relative path> ...      (required; may be empty)
#   DOCUMENT: <repo-relative path>            (optional; default fixture.md; sets the
#                                              directory a relative link resolves from)
#   <document lines>
#   --- END
# where
#   <EXPECT> = DRIFT       at least 1 DRIFT row and 0 UNRESOLVED rows
#            | CLEAN       at least 1 marker examined and 0 rows
#            | UNRESOLVED  at least 1 UNRESOLVED row and 0 DRIFT rows
#            | SCOPE-OUT   0 markers examined
#   <RELATION> = count | list | subset-of — the relation the case exercises (a label; a
#                malformed case cannot carry a parseable relation in its marker)
# POPULATION stands in for the tracked-file list, so a case runs with no git and no
# filesystem; the glob is matched against it exactly as against `git ls-files`.
#
# WHY EACH ARM IS LOAD-BEARING — read before tuning the tool against it.
# A CLEAN case that examines zero markers is a FAILURE, not a pass: "not flagged" and
# "not examined" are different verdicts, which is why SCOPE-OUT exists as its own
# expectation (the Check 63 fixture set's rule, reused). A DRIFT case that comes back
# UNRESOLVED is a FAILURE too: an unreadable marker is a finding, but it is not the drift
# the case seeds, and a tool that cannot bind the seeded list would pass a looser test.
#   - Cases 1 and 2 are the same items: only the relation differs. A tool that flags both
#     cannot tell `subset-of` from `list`; a tool that flags neither cannot see drift.
#   - Cases 3 to 6 pin each relation in both directions: an exact list, an extra member
#     under `subset-of`, an understated count, and a number word that reconciles.
#   - Case 7 pins segment-equal matching: a `*` that crossed `/` would make the nested
#     file a member and case 7 would drift.
#   - Cases 8 and 9 bound the preamble allowance at exactly one prose line.
#   - Cases 10 to 13 each seed one UNRESOLVED reason, so a marker the tool cannot read is
#     reported, never skipped as clean.
#   - Case 14 pins the fence rule: a marker quoted inside a fence is not a marker.
#   - Cases 15 and 16 pin wildcard-segment keys: every member is named SKILL.md, so a
#     basename key could neither key the list nor stay silent on the count.
#   - Cases 17 and 18 pin link resolution from the document's own directory, a leading
#     `/` from the root, and an off-glob link reading as extra rather than vanishing.
#   - Case 19 pins the code-span key of a glob with two wildcard segments.
#   - Case 20 pins the `dup` rule: every member is listed once and one is listed again,
#     so `missing` and `extra` are empty and only the repeat can drift. Case 3 is its
#     near-miss: the same list without the repeat.
#   - Case 21 pins the `**` limb of the malformed-glob rule: without the rule the glob is
#     read one level deep, so it silently drops pop/b/deep/run.sh, and the list, which
#     names both one-level members, reads CLEAN. Cases 26 and 27 pin its other two limbs.
#   - Case 22 pins table-body items: the header and separator rows are not items, so the
#     two body rows key alpha.sh and beta.sh, and gamma.sh is missing. Counted as items,
#     they make the item count disagree with the table's.
#   - Case 23 pins the strip of a `#...` fragment and of a `?...` query from a link target:
#     without either strip, that link no longer names a member.
#   - Case 24 pins code-span link masking: the item's first link sits inside a code span,
#     so its key comes from the real link after it.
#   - Case 25 pins the external-scheme limb of the link skip: the item's first link is
#     `https:`, so its key comes from its code span. Without the limb that link reads as
#     an extra path.
#   - Cases 26 and 27 pin the malformed-glob rule's leading-`/` and `..` limbs. Each
#     population carries paths of that shape, so the glob matches them: without its limb
#     the glob reads as an ordinary pattern and the list reads CLEAN, where the rule reads
#     `malformed-glob`.
#   - Case 28 pins the `~~~` limb of the fence rule, as case 14 pins the backtick limb:
#     without it the quoted marker is read, and its one-item list drifts.
#   - Case 29 pins reading the marker from the stripped line: indented by two spaces, it
#     is still a marker; read from the raw line, no marker is examined.
#   - Case 30 pins that a count does not bind a line that opens a list: the cardinal sits
#     in a list item, so the marker reads `count-target`; bound, the count reads CLEAN.
#   - Case 31 pins the masking of non-counting spans on a count line: the numeral inside
#     the code span is not a second cardinal; unmasked, the count reads UNRESOLVED.
#   - Cases 32 and 33 pin the blank-line skip after the marker, before a preamble line and
#     before a count line; without it the marker binds the blank line and reads UNRESOLVED.
#   - Case 34 pins the `dup` rule under `subset-of`, as case 20 pins it under `list`: a
#     repeated item drifts whatever the relation.
#   - Case 35 pins the prefix match of a resolved link: its leading segments must match
#     the glob's, so a link to ../lib/gamma.sh, a member's basename off the glob, reads as
#     the extra path lib/gamma.sh, with gamma.sh missing. Matched on the key alone, the
#     list reads CLEAN.
#   - Case 36 pins the segment floor of a resolved link: a link to the glob's directory,
#     pop/, is shorter than a member, so it reads as the extra path pop, with alpha.sh
#     missing. Without the floor the tool fails on an index past the path's end.
#   - Case 37 pins the full-path code span: a span with as many segments as the glob is
#     resolved as a path, so pop/alpha.sh keys alpha.sh; unresolved, it reads UNRESOLVED.
#   - Case 38 pins the strip of a trailing `/` from a code span: alpha/ keys the member
#     sk/alpha/SKILL.md; unstripped, it reads UNRESOLVED.
#   - Case 39 pins the key of a glob with no wildcard segment, which is its whole path;
#     without it the key is empty and the tool fails on an empty sequence.
#   - Case 40 pins the strip of a trailing `/` from a link target: a link to the root, /,
#     strips to nothing and is skipped; unstripped, it reads as an extra path.
# Not pinned by any case, and named so the set does not overstate its reach. Each is an
# equivalent mutant: removing it changes no verdict on any document, so no case can pin it.
#   - The `boundary-disagreement` verdict. The tool's item splitter computes the count by
#     the same steps as structure_at, so no document makes the two disagree, and the tool
#     with the verdict removed passes every case. It is a fail-closed assertion, reached
#     only through a splitter fault: with the table header counted as an item, case 22
#     reads `boundary-disagreement`.
#   - The pure-anchor limb of the link skip. The fragment strip already empties a `#...`
#     target, which is then skipped, so the tool with that limb removed passes every case.
# Two rules no case pins are not equivalents, since a case could pin each one, and only the
# `--self-test` kills them: `C-guard`, the ambiguity guard, by its `guard` arm, and
# `C-nested`, an item owning its nested lines, by its `parity` arm.
# Cases: 10 DRIFT · 19 CLEAN · 9 UNRESOLVED · 2 SCOPE-OUT — 40 in all.
